title: Looking to buy RPG Maker XP HD Battlebacks

posts.author: Glenn0705
posts.body:
Resource Type:
Battlebacks
Maker Format:
XP
Makers I Own:
XP, MV
Art Style:
XP RTP
Description:
I'm making a game in RPG Maker MV using the graphics of the XP RTP. I also have an XP license.
Lastly, I bought the VX Ace & XP Hero Pack, but I noticed the battlebacks still look grainy.
If anyone could point me in the direction of non-grainy XP Battlebacks (if the product exists anywhere, since I haven't been able to find it) I'd really appreciate it, since upscaling them makes them look kinda blurry.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
the problem is that the older makers (XP, VX, VXA) are/were limited to a maximum screen size of 640x480, so I highly doubt that there are any larger battlebacks available.
however the trick to a non-blurry upscaling is that the only non-blurry and non-distorted resize is full percentages (200%, 300%, and so on) with a nearest neighbour mathematic.
So to get the battlebacks you want you first need to scale the picture to a full percentage that is next larger to your intended game screen size, and then cut off (NOT resize) anything extra (keep a bit extra for screen shake effects)

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
If you're looking for the exact same battlebacks in higher resolution, unfortunately you're probably out of luck. XP was designed for 640x480, so all of its battlebacks will be sized for that--I've seen people remaster the music, but to my knowledge no one has manually scaled up the battlebacks.
Scaling up from XP (32px) to MV (48px) is difficult because it's only a 1.5x change, rather than a 2x change. It can be done (Avery is in the process of manually resizing the VXA tiles, with beautiful results) but it requires a lot more fussing to get something tidy.
If you aren't looking for those
exact
battlebacks, I think Avery has a tutorial for making MV resources match the MZ RTP, and you may be able to use the same core principles to adjust the MV battleback pieces to mimic the colors of the XP battlebacks!
(Could you link the XP Hero Pack? I don't think I've ever seen it, but it sounds interesting!)
Ninja'd by Andar XD Great suggestion for resizing by double and then cropping!

Thank you everyone very much for your input, sadly Andar I tried what you said but even upscaling by 200% and then cropping doesn't do the trick for me.
The thing is, I wanted to use these battlebacks as background art for VN-styled drawings or promotional art, not just battles, and in those cases it still looks too grainy/blurry compared to my game's art even if I upscale it by 200% nearest neighbor:
I thought they had made the original art at 1080p and had it downscaled to fit the average monitor's resolution at the time, and that's why I was wondering if we could find the original HD art somewhere, be it free or paid.
Also yeah I tried using RyanBram's upscaling tool that he published years ago, but the results weren't great either. I wanted to use the XP battlebacks because I really like the way XP's whole graphics and artstyle are more subdued in comparison to the imo oversatured look of the other Makers. But thank you TeiRaven and Avery, I'll check out the tutorials so I can edit the MV RTP and get the "subdued" style I'm looking for in HD.
Lastly the VX Ace & XP Hero Pack is this one, and it's absolutely worth it:
The enemies/characters have all been remade from the ground up and so have the sprites, which is why it surprised me that they didn't do the same for the battlebacks. But it's okay, I'll edit them then

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
For future reference, it would also be helpful for you to be more specific about the size of your game window that you want to match.
"HD" doesn't really have a definition beyond "taller than 480," so the battlebacks that come with MV and MZ (1000x740) are already "HD." If you specifically want 1920x1080 or some other size, it's best to say so.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Avery said:
unless you use some kind of AI which is a grey area that is frowned upon here.
Click to expand...
AI upscalers, such as Waifu2x have been around long before every marketing and PR department started frothing at the mouth of "AI enabled gimmickry", and afaik, are not based on LLM nor diffusion models that current AI models use.
Basically, it might be a grey area because lots of people spontaneously combust at the mere mention of those 2 dreaded letters, but in truth is far more ethical in it's usage.
I would say, that scalers like Waifu2x were built for upscaling old anime, and as a result tend to produce the best results with cartoon-styled graphics, so maybe this would be worth an attempt at AI upscaling.
The results are passable. You might want to play around with noise reduction setting some more.
Here, I scaled it up by 2x with low noise reduction applied:
and then I fed that into Waifu2x again and scaled it up by another 2x with medium noise reduction.
At this point, the AI does start to fall apart a little bit, but maybe only if you are pixel peeping. Anyways, I think 2x is probably the best result.
But, for what it is worth, I really like Avery's stylish effect, with the normal resolution in front and a simple scaled up and blurred version in back. It looks quite nice.
I know you want to use these for VN stuff, but I am sure you could apply a similar idea to the VN stuff as well.
